evidence: Receiving DO2 at 50.0 h = 10.66 mg/L then 4.56 mg/L at 50.2 h, falling to 3.70 mg/L at 52.0 h
All three source batches and receiving history before 50 h never fell below ~7.4 mg/L; receiving batch at 52 h is at 3.70 mg/L
Physics tool: KEEP min DO 1.51 mg/L (infeasible), increase_air 1.38, combined 1.47, reduce_feed 1.44 — all infeasible
Physics tool: strong_feed_reduction min DO 2.18 mg/L, 0 h below limit, product mass ~241 kg vs 198 kg KEEP, 4/5 sensitivity members feasible
Constraint: minimum DO2 operating limit 2.0 mg/L; allowed_actions strong_feed_reduction = [0.6 feed, 1.15 air]
submission.rationale: The receiving fermentation entered an oxygen-transfer deficit at ~50 h (DO2 fell from ~10.7 to ~3.7 mg/L within 2 h), unlike the source batches where comparable DO2 dips recovered. The forward model calibrated to the receiving state estimates an oxygen transfer multiplier of ~0.51 and predicts KEEP, increase_air, reduce_feed, and combined all violate the 2.0 mg/L minimum-DO constraint (minimum DO 1.4–1.5 mg/L, 3.6–5.2 h below limit), while strong_feed_reduction (0.6× feed, 1.15× air) keeps minimum DO at ~2.18 mg/L with zero below-limit hours and yields the highest product mass (~241 kg vs ~198 kg for KEEP). It is the only bounded intervention that is predicted feasible and retains/grows product mass; a stop would count zero production. Note the model is an imperfect source-calibrated prediction and one of five sensitivity members still breaches the limit, so close DO2 monitoring is advised after implementation.
submission.uncertainty: Moderate-to-high: forward-model predictions are source-calibrated, not the hidden receiving realization; sensitivity members span min DO 1.30–2.82 mg/L under strong_feed_reduction (4/5 feasible). The abrupt DO2 step at 50.2 h could partly reflect a sensor fault, but the sustained decline to 3.7 mg/L supports a real deficit. Hidden kinetics/feed state could make the milder combined action sufficient, but the risk of an oxygen-constraint violation and product loss under those actions is higher.

evidence: Receiving DO2 sensor at t=52.0 h: 3.695 mg/L, after collapse from 10.66 mg/L at t=50.0 h (sudden step drop starting t=50.2)
Minimum DO constraint is 2.0 mg/L; extrapolation reaches it in ~3-4 h under KEEP
Source batches (source-1,2,3) at t=52 h show DO2 ~10.5-11.5 mg/L, confirming receiving deviation is abnormal
Receiving P assay (delayed) t=48 h: 2.80 g/L and rising - production mass retained, stop rejected
Allowed action bounds: combined = feed 0.8, air 1.15, within permitted ranges
submission.rationale: The receiving fermentation shows an abrupt DO2 collapse from ~10.7 mg/L at t=50.0 h to 3.7 mg/L at t=52.0 h (falling ~0.5 mg/L/h), unlike source batches which held ~10.5-11.5 mg/L at the same age. If DO2 continues at this slope it breaches the 2.0 mg/L minimum within ~3-4 h. increase_air alone (max 1.15x) directly raises oxygen transfer and is the fastest way to lift DO2 above the constraint; the 0.8x feed reduction reduces oxygen demand so the DO recovery is sustained and does not rely solely on the bounded air increase. The 20% feed cut retains most production capacity (P was still rising, 2.80 g/L at t=48 assay), unlike a stop (zero counted production) or a strong 40% feed cut. KEEP alone carries a high probability of an oxygen-constraint violation. Combined bounded intervention best balances constraint safety with product-mass retention.
submission.uncertainty: Exact air-transfer gain from 1.15x air and the kinetics of demand reduction from a 0.8x feed cut are unknown (hidden parameters), so the speed of DO2 recovery is uncertain; the DO2 drop could also partly reflect viscosity or mixing effects that air increase only partially offsets. The 48-h P assay lags current state by 4 h, so true current titer is uncertain. If the collapse were a sensor artifact, the feed reduction would cost some productivity - but the consistent multi-point decline (10 points over 1.8 h) makes artifact unlikely.
